goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 — Making .small-action a flex container causes its direct button's float:right to be ignored, so action controls no longer stay right-aligned.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that .small-action is being converted to a flex container with @include flexbox() and @include align-items(center). In CSS, when an element becomes a flex container, float properties on its direct children are ignored. The finding claims there's a button with float:right that would be affected. While the diff doesn't show the button's CSS directly, this is a well-known CSS behavior issue. The diff does show other float-related changes being made (e.g., removing float:left from .title, replacing float:right with margin-left:auto and order() in .panel), suggesting the author is aware of this issue in some places but may have missed it for .small-action's button children.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:124 — order($val)` passes modern zero-based order values directly to legacy `box-ordinal-group`, whose values are one-based, so its abstraction yields divergent ordering across supported flexbox implementations

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the `order($val)` mixin at lines 127-133 passes the same `$val` to both modern `order` (zero-based) and legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` (one-based). When `@include order(2)` or `@include order(3)` is called (as seen in topic.scss and header.scss), the legacy box-ordinal-group properties receive the same value, but they expect 1-based indexing. This means `order: 2` should map to `box-ordinal-group: 3` for equivalent behavior. The mixin doesn't account for this offset, causing inconsistent ordering in older browsers that use the legacy flexbox spec.
